claims.quote: You can apply for a Debt Relief Order or Bankruptcy Order if you cannot pay your debts because you do not have enough money or assets you can sell.
claims.note: The text says you lack enough money or assets to pay your debts, but does not set a test that debts must exceed assets.

claims.claim: The person must be unable to pay debts as they fall due.
claims.quote: the debtor is unable to pay his or her debts at the date of the determination
claims.note: The Act requires the debtor to be unable to pay their debts, but the 'as they fall due' wording is not in the text.

claims.claim: The bankruptcy trustee may sell assets.
claims.quote: If your possessions are valuable, the trustee may sell them. This can include selling your home but only if you have equity in it.
claims.note: The text says the trustee may sell valuable possessions, including the home if there is equity.

claims.claim: Owning significant property is a reason bankruptcy may not be suitable.
claims.quote: The things you own may be sold to pay for your bankruptcy and make payments towards your debts. This can sometimes include selling your home .
claims.note: The text warns that property may be sold, but does not present owning significant property as something that excludes you or makes bankruptcy unsuitable.
